Checked the weather map and started driving. As usually, nothing goes as planned, I ended up driving further more than I wanted, along a huge lighting storm system and eventually I was able to pass the storm and catch up with Lady Aurora after 180 Km driving along. I was able to witness some colorful pillars and some green for about 30 minutes. After that, the hell broke loose, the lighting storm took over the sky and also the data died…The Northern Lights, the lighting storm combined with the clouds and some light pollution created an incredible and surreal night. It was not visible to the naked eye and photographs would not have shown that it was behaving very differently from a typical auroral curtain. The basic behaviour of this aurora was to appear, move upwards like a pulsating wave or curtain, then disappear when it reached the highest point. These discrete flames sometimes occurred several times a second, but more often were once every second or two, in different locations but mostly grouped in one area. The individual flames lasted from around 1/10 of a second, but ocassionally lasted over a second, maybe up to two second.  I think this was a very unusual aurora. The photo I included is a poor representation of it and just looks like a dim curtain, please see the video.

height_other: Activity was visible shortly after nautical twilight, formed by one large diffuse band to the south and arcing aurora overhead, stretching from east to west. Around 2230-2300 aurora activity exploded, starting from overhead. The aurora became very bright, stretching down from zenith over the course of 5 minutes generating large, dynamic curtains of aurora with easily detectable colors of red, green, pink, and purple to the unaided eye. This intense period of activity was roughly maintained for approximately 45 minutes until the intensity would begin to wane. After midnight, the activity would begin to concentrate across more of the northern hemisphere of the sky and be primarily made up of 10-20 min flares of arc aurora and widespread, constant diffuse and patchy aurora. Color was visible periodically with flares. Diffuse and patchy aurora was maintaining once observation ceased around 330.
activities_other: Aurora was very active with significant blurring occurring in 6 sec exposures. Most aggressive motion occurred later in the night with the diffuse and patchy aurora. Significant large motion occurred when aurora peaked while looking at zenith. Motion would occur in sub-second intervals with aurora arcing, disappearing, and being generated. Over peak and at end of night, secondary shimmering/pulsation would occur in aurora structure, emanating uniformly from the north across all aurora occurring.
types_other: Night alternated between discrete arcs and diffuse glow until approx 130-200, where there was patch-like aurora across the northern hemisphere of the sky. Patch-like aurora also demonstrated a uniform "pulsing" of intensity resembling a dull, but near periodic, shimmer across all aurora. Diffuse ovaline blobs of red were also seen periodically through the night.

Or are they some other phenomena associated with the aurora? This is not an artifact from my camera, such as a malfunctioning camera chip.  I took photos from two sepatae cameras and these patches could be seen in both cameras.  The attached photo shows these patches.  Has anyone seen these before?
